brief: A weak 5-year Treasury auction (5.033%, first 5-handle since 2007, second-biggest tail on record, lowest bid-to-cover since 2018) pushed yields to multi-decade highs: the 10Y briefly topped 5.3%, the 30Y cleared 5.6%, and the MOVE index spiked above 100. Equities ignored it, with the Nasdaq rallying over 3% last week on Meta's Muse AI assistant. BofA argues macro risk is losing the competition for investor attention against AI growth narratives, a dynamic it calls the 'AI put,' noting that in the 1990s long-end rates rose 200bps and the Fed hiked 100bps while the dot-com bubble kept inflating. The real risk BofA flags is the reverse: an AI-narrative hiccup would remove the hope that AI productivity hedges fiscal unsustainability, amplifying macro stress and creating real equity risk, though BofA sees that risk as further out given still-strong fundamentals and narrow bubble-indicator breadth. BofA recommends NDX calls on a rates-higher-but-range-bound view, TLT put spreads, and put spreads on XLB/IWM/XLY, while its stress indicator shows rates vol, FX and credit all deteriorating even as equities stay calm.
